title: Women and children first
eyebrow: CETI · a data film · the Titanic, April 1912
lede: A ship's manifest as a city of 2,201 boxes, one per person aboard. Pooled, the rule held: women and children lived far more often than men. Re-berthed by class, the same boxes show a third-class child lived as often as a first-class man.

knobs_doc.name: caseT0
knobs_doc.what: s: film time at which the stack-city clock starts (CASE t0); the module's local time is t - caseT0

knobs_doc.name: caseT1
knobs_doc.what: s: film time at which the stack-city clock ends (CASE t1); beats below are converted to fractions of caseT1 - caseT0

knobs_doc.name: arrive0
knobs_doc.what: s: the first person boards (boxes start dropping into the three pooled columns)

knobs_doc.name: arrive1
knobs_doc.what: s: the last person has boarded; must be <= count.at 24.0 so 2,201 is landed before any ratio

knobs_doc.name: arrW
knobs_doc.what: fraction of the CASE clock one box takes to fall and grow into its berth (larger = softer arrival)

knobs_doc.name: drop
knobs_doc.what: world units a box falls from as it arrives (0 = boxes appear in place)

knobs_doc.name: lit0
knobs_doc.what: s: survivors start to light, bottom-up in every column

knobs_doc.name: lit1
knobs_doc.what: s: every survivor is lit (the LIVED row of the ledger lands)

knobs_doc.name: poolPins
knobs_doc.what: s: the pooled pins appear with their counts (N OF M)

knobs_doc.name: ratioDelay
knobs_doc.what: s: a pin's % waits this long after its count (floor 1.5: counts before ratios)

knobs_doc.name: poolOut
knobs_doc.what: s: the pooled pins fade before the re-berthing starts

knobs_doc.name: move0
knobs_doc.what: s: the boxes leave the pooled columns for their class berths

knobs_doc.name: move1
knobs_doc.what: s: the last box is in its class berth

knobs_doc.name: stagger
knobs_doc.what: 0-1: how spread out in time the boxes leave (0 = all at once; each box keeps its own path)

knobs_doc.name: lift
knobs_doc.what: world units: height of the arc each box makes between its two berths

knobs_doc.name: orderMix
knobs_doc.what: 0 = seeded order, 1 = class order (the berths fill one class after another)

knobs_doc.name: berth0
knobs_doc.what: s: the class berths start to show as outlines on the deck (the empty crew-children berth among them)

knobs_doc.name: berth1
knobs_doc.what: s: the berth outlines are fully drawn

knobs_doc.name: berthOp
knobs_doc.what: 0-1: opacity of the berth outlines

knobs_doc.name: tag0
knobs_doc.what: s: the two followed people (a third-class child, a first-class man) take the accent and a riding pin

knobs_doc.name: tag1
knobs_doc.what: s: the followed people return to their group colour; pins off

knobs_doc.name: turn0
knobs_doc.what: s: the camera starts its turn (keep equal to move0: the turn and the re-berthing are one gesture)

knobs_doc.name: turn1
knobs_doc.what: s: the camera arrives at the berth view

knobs_doc.name: az0
knobs_doc.what: degrees: azimuth of the pooled view (0 = straight on the three columns)

knobs_doc.name: az1
knobs_doc.what: degrees: azimuth of the berth view (90 = square on to the class row)

knobs_doc.name: elev0
knobs_doc.what: degrees: elevation of the pooled view (higher shows more roofs)

knobs_doc.name: elev1
knobs_doc.what: degrees: elevation of the berth view (lower flattens the row, higher separates labels)

knobs_doc.name: orbitAmp
knobs_doc.what: degrees: amplitude of the calm orbit sway, the whole film (0 = still camera)

knobs_doc.name: orbitPeriod
knobs_doc.what: s: period of the calm orbit sway (longer = slower)

knobs_doc.name: fit0
knobs_doc.what: ortho extent multiplier in the pooled view (larger = further away)

knobs_doc.name: fit1
knobs_doc.what: ortho extent multiplier in the berth view (larger = further away)

knobs_doc.name: fitReveal
knobs_doc.what: multiplier on the extent during the reveal (below 1 = a slow push in)

knobs_doc.name: lookY
knobs_doc.what: 0-1 of the city height the camera looks at (larger moves the city down the frame)

knobs_doc.name: boxSize
knobs_doc.what: world units: edge of one person's box

knobs_doc.name: boxGap
knobs_doc.what: world units: seam between boxes

knobs_doc.name: slabLayers
knobs_doc.what: boxes high a class berth is (rate form: every berth the same height, so lit height = share who lived)

knobs_doc.name: slabDepth
knobs_doc.what: boxes deep a class berth is (along the view axis of the berth view)

knobs_doc.name: slabGap
knobs_doc.what: world units: aisle between classes

knobs_doc.name: pairGap
knobs_doc.what: world units: gap between the women, children and men berths of one class

knobs_doc.name: groupGap
knobs_doc.what: world units: gap between the three pooled columns

knobs_doc.name: poolLayers
knobs_doc.what: boxes high a pooled column is (rate form: width = how many, lit height = share who lived)

knobs_doc.name: poolDepth
knobs_doc.what: boxes deep a pooled column is

knobs_doc.name: deckPad
knobs_doc.what: world units: deck margin around the berths

knobs_doc.name: planks
knobs_doc.what: number of plank seams across the deck (0 = plain deck)

knobs_doc.name: dim
knobs_doc.what: 0-1: how far a person who did not live is mixed toward the deck (larger = darker)

knobs_doc.name: maskDim
knobs_doc.what: 0-1: how far everyone outside the counted pair dims during the reveal

knobs_doc.name: ambient
knobs_doc.what: fill light on every face (display-linear multiplier)

knobs_doc.name: keyLight
knobs_doc.what: key light from above-left (display-linear multiplier)

knobs_doc.name: rimLight
knobs_doc.what: rim light from behind-right (display-linear multiplier)

knobs_doc.name: deckMix
knobs_doc.what: 0-1: deck colour from ground (0) to panel (1)

knobs_doc.name: plankMix
knobs_doc.what: 0-1: plank seam colour from ground toward muted

knobs_doc.name: berthMix
knobs_doc.what: 0-1: berth outline colour from ground toward accent

knobs_doc.name: hold
knobs_doc.what: frames a label must be pushed before it hides (gl-labels hysteresis)

knobs_doc.name: leader
knobs_doc.what: sheet units: leader length of a slab pin

knobs_doc.name: maxShown
knobs_doc.what: label budget per frame (manager: 12)

knobs_doc.name: pinLift
knobs_doc.what: world units: a pin's anchor above its berth's roof

knobs_doc.name: pinSize
knobs_doc.what: sheet units: slab pin type (secondary floor 14)

knobs_doc.name: poolPinSize
knobs_doc.what: sheet units: pooled pin type (result floor 28)

knobs_doc.name: calloutSize
knobs_doc.what: sheet units: callout type (result)

knobs_doc.name: calloutLeader
knobs_doc.what: sheet units: callout leader length

knobs_doc.name: revealSize
knobs_doc.what: sheet units: the two reveal results

knobs_doc.name: per10Size
knobs_doc.what: sheet units: the natural-frequency line in the reveal

knobs_doc.name: plate
knobs_doc.what: 0-1: opacity of the dark plate behind a pin's text

knobs_doc.name: chromeDim
knobs_doc.what: opacity of the slab pins the callout does not name

knobs_doc.name: dispAdv
knobs_doc.what: em: average advance of the display face, for label boxes

knobs_doc.name: slabPins
knobs_doc.what: s: the eleven slab pins enter with their counts

knobs_doc.name: call0
knobs_doc.what: s: callout on the first- and second-class children

knobs_doc.name: call1
knobs_doc.what: s: callout hard cuts to the third-class children

knobs_doc.name: call2
knobs_doc.what: s: callout hard cuts to the first-class men

knobs_doc.name: callEnd
knobs_doc.what: s: the callout ends before the reveal

knobs_doc.name: crewAt
knobs_doc.what: s: the slab pins return and the callout names the crew men

knobs_doc.name: reveal0
knobs_doc.what: s: everyone outside the counted pair starts to dim

knobs_doc.name: reveal1
knobs_doc.what: s: the dim is complete

knobs_doc.name: revealPins
knobs_doc.what: s: the two results appear (labels after post, flat)

knobs_doc.name: per10At
knobs_doc.what: s: the natural-frequency line appears

knobs_doc.name: revealEnd0
knobs_doc.what: s: the reveal starts to lift

knobs_doc.name: revealEnd1
knobs_doc.what: s: the reveal has lifted (crew beat)

knobs_doc.name: postLevel
knobs_doc.what: gl-post level: exec = tone map only; manager = bloom, vignette (and dof)

knobs_doc.name: bloomGain
knobs_doc.what: bloom strength on the counted pair (0.04-0.12 typical; 0 = off)

knobs_doc.name: bloom0
knobs_doc.what: s: bloom starts to rise (after the dim, so only the counted pair glows)

knobs_doc.name: bloom1
knobs_doc.what: s: bloom at full gain

knobs_doc.name: bloom2
knobs_doc.what: s: bloom starts to fall

knobs_doc.name: bloom3
knobs_doc.what: s: bloom off

knobs_doc.name: glowGain
knobs_doc.what: emission of the counted pair's lit boxes in the reveal (> 1 glows)

knobs_doc.name: vignetteGain
knobs_doc.what: corner darkening in the reveal window

knobs_doc.name: dofGain
knobs_doc.what: depth of field (0 = off: ortho scene, and it costs ~0.5 s/frame)

knobs_doc.name: exposure
knobs_doc.what: pre-tonemap exposure, the whole film

knobs_doc.name: monday0
knobs_doc.what: s: the city starts to dim for Monday

knobs_doc.name: monday1
knobs_doc.what: s: the city is at Monday exposure

knobs_doc.name: mondayExposure
knobs_doc.what: exposure of the city under the Monday question

knobs_doc.name: mondayGlow
knobs_doc.what: emission of the counted pair under the Monday question (a faint glow, no bloom)

knobs_doc.name: hookAt
knobs_doc.what: s: the rule starts to type

knobs_doc.name: hookCps
knobs_doc.what: characters per second the rule types

knobs_doc.name: hookOut
knobs_doc.what: s: the rule fades before the first person boards

knobs_doc.name: hookSize
knobs_doc.what: sheet units: the rule (display face)

knobs_doc.name: ledgerSize
knobs_doc.what: sheet units: ledger numbers (must-read)

knobs_doc.name: ledgerDim
knobs_doc.what: opacity of the ledger once the re-berthing starts

knobs_doc.name: ledgerOut
knobs_doc.what: s: the ledger leaves (before the slab pins, which need its corner)

knobs_doc.name: mondaySize
knobs_doc.what: sheet units: the Monday question

chapters.title: Which group does it leave out?

captions: “Women and children first.” The rule everyone remembers.
Did it hold that night for every child aboard?
The Titanic, April 1912. One box is one person aboard.
Passengers and crew: everyone the inquiry counted.
2,201 people. Lit boxes are the ones who lived.
711 lived. 1,490 did not.
Lived: 316 of 425 women, 57 of 109 children, 338 of 1,667 men.
Women and children together: 373 of 534, or 70 %. Men: 20 %.
On average the rule held. Now split the same 2,201 by class.
First, second, third class and the crew. No box added or removed.
Each slab: how many were aboard, and how many lived.
Children in first and second class: 30 of 30 lived.
Children in third class: 27 of 79 lived. 52 did not.
Men in first class: 57 of 175 lived.
34 % and 33 %: a third-class child lived as often as a first-class man.
About 3 in 10 of each. Class weighed as much as being a child.
The crew: 885 people, 40 % of everyone aboard. 212 lived.
Of the 1,667 men, 1,324 were crew or third class. The men’s 20 % is mostly them.
Monday: your “on average” result. Which group does it leave out?
One night, one inquiry’s count: it shows who lived, not why.

brand.takeaway: True on average is not true for every group.

sources: Dawson, R. J. MacG. (1995). The “Unusual Episode” data revisited. Journal of Statistics Education 3(3). The 32 cells (transcribed from memory in the brief lane; verify before public use).
British Board of Trade, Wreck Commissioner (Lord Mersey) (1912). Report on the Loss of the “Titanic” (S.S.). London: HMSO.
R Core Team. datasets::Titanic, Survival of passengers on the Titanic (R documentation): 2,201 observations, source Dawson (1995).
Rdatasets (V. Arel-Bundock), csv/datasets/Titanic.csv (pydataset 0.2.0 copy): a secondary cross-check, 32 of 32 cells agree.
Simonoff, J. S. (1997). The “unusual episode” and a second statistics course. Journal of Statistics Education 5(1).
honest: One night, one inquiry's count: it shows who lived, not why (deck, boats, language and order of arrival are not in the table; primary sources disagree on the exact numbers aboard).
